items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: His name was Arthur Horn. And he taught me everything he was able to teach me

ctx.x: the people to the medicine show, and... There was always plenty of music around, you know.

Yes, and I'd like to get back to the very beginning of my association with the instrument. There was a saxophone player living at our house, renting a room. You know, in ...(?)... plenty of rooms, and two beds in one room and all that type of thing. And he lived there with us... So my mother approached him about teaching me to play, giving me lessons. And he was very happy to do it. And they came to an agreement where she washed and ironed his clothes to pay for my lesson, 35 cents per lesson, you know. His name…

So I was pretty much on my own, and practicing out of the books; you know, the original saxophone book, the Ben Barekan(?) -- because all the guys were studying out of that. I think a lot of guys nowadays... In fact, I heard John Coltrane play a passage the other day from that book. [LAUGHS] I noticed some little lines in there. You know, a lot of guys lifted those lines out of that book. There are some pretty good lines in the book.
